hooks.prompt:
You are reviewing ONE edit against this repo's self-documenting-code principles. The hook payload is: $ARGUMENTS

Read tool_input.file_path and the text this edit ADDS (tool_input.new_string for Edit, tool_input.content for Write, the edits array for MultiEdit).

Respond ok immediately, with no further analysis, if ANY of these hold:
- the file is not source code (only .ts, .tsx, .js, .jsx, .cs count)
- the edit adds no comments and no new identifier names

Otherwise judge ONLY the text this edit adds. A comment is earned when it explains something the code cannot: a non-obvious WHY, a complex edge case, or a warning that stops someone undoing a deliberate decision.

Fail only when an ADDED comment clearly does one of these:
- restates what the adjacent code already says, or narrates the steps it performs
- explains a rule that a config file already defines (prettier, eslint, tsconfig, commitlint)
- embeds a count, statistic or file tally that will go stale
- compensates for an unclear name, where renaming or extracting a named function would serve better

Also fail if the edit introduces an abbreviated identifier name where a full word was available.

Bias strongly toward ok: this runs on every edit and false positives are worse than misses. Judge only what was added, never pre-existing code. When failing, quote the specific comment or name and give a one-sentence reason.
